title: The Self-Testing Agent Desk
pitch: chrome-devtools-mcp lets an AI coding agent open a real browser, click through a page, and catch broken buttons or console errors on its own; Plannotator gives a team one shared inbox to watch, comment on, and redirect everything their agents produce. Wire the two together and every agent-built feature arrives in the review inbox with its own screenshots, console log, and a pass/fail note already attached, because the agent tested itself in a live browser before asking for human eyes. A reviewer spends their click approving visual proof instead of re-running the app themselves. Package this as a 'self-testing agent desk' and sell it to dev agencies and small product teams running multiple coding agents who want fewer surprises landing in their review queue.
why_now: Both repos trended the same week because teams running AI coding agents at scale have hit the same two walls back to back: agents write UI code blind, and humans can't keep up with reviewing everything agents produce. One tool fixes the blind-testing problem, the other fixes the review-bottleneck problem — chaining them turns 'agent wrote code, hope it works' into 'agent wrote code, proved it works, human just signs off.'
